title: Free Techniques to Avoid Spam Filters and Improve Your Deliverability
summary: Master email deliverability: authenticate, maintain sender reputation, and engage organically for top inbox placement in 2025!
body_markdown:
## Free Technical Wins You Can Apply in Minutes


### Publish SPF, DKIM, and DMARC


[Set up SPF records](https://themailx.com/) to specify which servers are allowed to send email for your domain. Implement **DKIM** signing with a 2048‑bit key to boost message authenticity. Add **DMARC** with *p=none* as a starting point so you can monitor email flows. Direct the *rua* value to a mailbox you check. Ensuring your visible From domain matches your authenticated domain costs nothing and proves your sender identity.


### Align Domains and Headers


Spam filters reward alignment: your *Return‑Path* , *DKIM d=* domain, and visible From domain should match. Keep your From name constant and avoid using aliases while warming up your sender reputation; filters trust consistency.


### Set Reverse DNS and a Clean HELO


Map your sending IP to a hostname using a PTR record. Make sure your SMTP banner matches this hostname. When possible, enable TLS for your email. These small steps eliminate technical doubts about your authenticity.


### Include a Plain‑Text Part


Send emails in multipart format, containing both HTML and plain text. Your text part should be thoughtfully written, avoid leaving it blank or using placeholder text, since filters evaluate both versions.


### Skip Link Shorteners


Link shorteners often come with a bad reputation. Use direct links that are visible and clearly associated with your brand to maintain trust.


## Build and Protect Your Sender Reputation Without Paying


### Start Small and Ramp Gradually


Begin sending at a low daily volume and increase your sends in small increments every few days. If you encounter bounces or blocks, maintain your current level before trying to grow again. Exercising such volume discipline is an effective and cost-free way to build trust.


### Keep Your List Clean


Remove invalid email addresses as soon as a hard bounce occurs. **Hard bounces** mean that the email has been returned to you because the recipient’s address is invalid. Suppress role-based accounts such as *info@* or *admin@* during warm up. Regularly prune dormant contacts who never open or respond to your emails. Steer clear of purchased or scraped lists, as they can quickly destroy your sending reputation.


### Encourage Safe, Organic Engagement


Invite genuine contacts to reply to your first emails. Ask them to move any misplaced messages from Spam to Inbox and even star the conversation. These real engagement signals tell spam filters your messages have value.


### Keep a Steady Cadence


Send on a predictable schedule. Avoid sending large bursts from new domains. Maintaining a pattern of slow, steady growth in email sending volume appears more trustworthy to spam filters.


## Manual Warm Up That Actually Works


You can manually warm up a new sending domain with a straightforward plan that only costs your time. Follow the steps below:


1. Create a small pool of trustworthy recipients you know.
2. Start by sending five to ten emails per day.
3. Write short, genuine messages that encourage replies.
4. Ask recipients to reply in complete sentences, not just one or two words.
5. Have them mark your emails as important or star them.
6. If a message goes to Spam, request that recipients move it to their Inbox.
7. Increase your daily sends in small increments each week.
8. Rotate message topics to keep email threads natural and varied.


This manual routine generates positive signals, like opens, replies, and ongoing conversations, that train filters to trust your sender. It also helps you identify deliverability issues early. For a deeper breakdown, see our guide on the differences between[manual and automatic email warm-up approaches](https://www.mailwarm.com/blog/manual-automatic-email-warmup) .


## Content and Sending Practices Filters Like


Write subject lines that are clear and descriptive, avoid excessive punctuation or all-caps. Always use a real email signature with your name and domain. Keep attachments small and never send executable files. The overall message size should stay under a few megabytes.


Whenever possible, include only one primary link domain in your email. Ensure your footers and addresses are consistent between sends. Always provide recipients with an easy and visible way to unsubscribe from your list, a frictionless exit reduces complaint rates.


Avoid using misleading language or promises of quick riches in your content. Filters are skeptical of pushy sales tactics and deception. Be clear and straightforward about your offer, authenticity earns trust.


## Monitor Signals and Fix Issues Quickly


### Watch Bounces and Blocks


**Hard bounces** mean that the email has been returned to the sender because the recipient’s address is invalid. If this happens, remove the recipient’s email address from your list immediately. Soft bounces usually indicate temporary problems or rate limits, wait and try again later if you see them. Email blocks can signal issues with either your reputation or sending practices. If blocks occur, pause your mailings and investigate the root cause.


### Use Free Postmaster Tools


Gmail Postmaster Tools let you track sender reputation trends over time; set it up with your domain to get insight. DMARC aggregate reports can also be a helpful tool. They provide valuable information about who is sending email on your behalf, enabling you to understand and regulate the use of your outbound email domain. Quickly address any unknown sources sending from your domain.


### Log Everything


Maintain a record of each send, date, volume, recipient domain, and results. Note any complaints or blocks. Even a simple spreadsheet will reveal useful patterns quickly once information is consistently recorded.

## Quick, Free Checklist


- Publish SPF, DKIM, and DMARC with domain alignment.
- Set reverse DNS and a consistent SMTP (HELO) banner.
- Send multipart emails with a genuine text part.
- Avoid link shorteners and mismatched link domains.
- Start with low volume, gradually increase, and keep a steady cadence.
- Promptly remove hard bounces and avoid risky data sources.
- Seek replies from trusted contacts during the warm up phase.
- Monitor bounces, complaints, and postmaster dashboards.
- Document every change and result after each send.


Follow this checklist in sequence, most steps can be done in just minutes. Collectively, these actions will strengthen your sender reputation and improve inbox placement.


## Conclusion: Free Techniques Can Boost Your Email Deliverability


With diligence and a simple strategy, free tactics can help new domains achieve strong sender reputation and reliable inbox placement. Begin by establishing identity, then focus on maintaining steady sending practices and building engagement. Keep documentation to track your progress. ## FAQ


What are SPF, DKIM, and DMARC and why are they important?


SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are authentication protocols that help verify your email sender identity, reducing the risk of your emails being marked as spam. Implementing these protocols shows that your emails are legitimate and increases the likelihood of successful delivery to the inbox.


Why is it important to maintain a consistent email sending pattern?


Consistency in email sending patterns helps build trust with spam filters. Sudden changes, like large increases in email volume, can raise red flags and lead to emails being flagged as spam.


How can I keep my email list clean?


Regularly remove invalid addresses that result in hard bounces, and avoid using purchased or scraped lists. Suppressing role-based accounts and pruning inactive contacts also help maintain a clean list.


What are some best practices for email content to avoid being marked as spam?


Use clear, descriptive subject lines and avoid excessive punctuation or caps. Ensure that your emails have a genuine plain-text version and avoid misleading language or overly aggressive sales tactics.


How does manual email warm-up work?


Manual email warm-up involves gradually increasing your email sending volume. You start with a small group of trusted recipients and slowly add more, generating positive engagement signals like replies and opens.


Why should I avoid using link shorteners in emails?


Link shorteners can have a bad reputation with spam filters, as they mask the final destination of the link. Using direct and clearly branded links helps maintain trust with both recipients and filters.


How can I monitor and address deliverability issues?


Monitoring tools like Gmail Postmaster Tools can provide insights into your sender reputation and identify potential issues. Keep track of bounce rates and any blocks, and promptly investigate the causes to address them quickly.
